steps.title: Import HttpClientModule and necessary Angular modules
steps.instruction: In your app.module.ts file, import HttpClientModule from '@angular/common/http' and add it to the imports array of the AppModule.
steps.hint: You need to import HttpClientModule to enable HTTP functionality in your Angular application.
steps.expectedOutcome: HttpClientModule will be imported and added to the AppModule imports array, enabling HTTP client functionality throughout the application.
successCriteria: HttpClientModule is imported from '@angular/common/http' and included in the imports array of AppModule.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported HttpClientModule, which is essential for making HTTP requests in Angular.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure HttpClientModule is both imported and added to the imports array in the @NgModule decorator.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you've imported HttpClientModule from '@angular/common/http' and added it to the imports array in AppModule.

steps.title: Create a data service with HttpClient
steps.instruction: Generate a new Angular service named 'DataService' that will handle HTTP requests. Use the Angular CLI command 'ng generate service data' or manually create a service file with HttpClient injection.
steps.hint: A service is a TypeScript class decorated with @Injectable(). Inject HttpClient in the constructor to make HTTP requests.
steps.expectedOutcome: A DataService class is created with HttpClient injected in its constructor, ready for HTTP operations.
successCriteria: DataService is a TypeScript class decorated with @Injectable, has HttpClient injected in constructor, and is exported.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the DataService with HttpClient injection. This service will be the foundation for making HTTP requests in your application.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your service includes: 1) @Injectable() decorator, 2) HttpClient injection in constructor, 3) proper export statement.
steps.feedbackWrong: The service structure isn't quite right. Remember to create a class named DataService with @Injectable() decorator and HttpClient injection.

steps.title: Define an interface for the response data
steps.instruction: In your DataService file, create a TypeScript interface named 'ApiResponse' that describes the structure of data you expect from the API. For this lesson, define it with a 'message' property of type string.
steps.hint: Use the 'interface' keyword followed by the interface name and define the properties inside curly braces.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a TypeScript interface that provides type safety for the API response data.
successCriteria: An interface named 'ApiResponse' is defined with a 'message' property of type string.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the ApiResponse interface. This will ensure type safety when working with the API response data.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your interface is named exactly 'ApiResponse' and has a 'message' property of type string.
steps.feedbackWrong: The interface definition is missing or incorrect. Remember to use the 'interface' keyword, name it 'ApiResponse', and include a 'message: string' property.

steps.title: Implement a fetch method in the service
steps.instruction: In your DataService, create a method named 'fetchData' that returns an Observable of ApiResponse using HttpClient.get().
steps.hint: Inject HttpClient in the constructor and use its get method with a URL. The return type should be Observable<ApiResponse>.
steps.expectedOutcome: The DataService will have a fetchData method that makes an HTTP GET request and returns an Observable typed to ApiResponse.
successCriteria: DataService has a fetchData method returning Observable<ApiResponse> using HttpClient.get.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! Your fetchData method is correctly implemented with proper typing and HttpClient usage.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Ensure the method returns Observable<ApiResponse> and uses HttpClient.get with a URL.
steps.feedbackWrong: The method is missing or incorrect. Check the method name, return type, and HttpClient usage.

steps.title: Create a component to display fetched data
steps.instruction: Create a new Angular component named 'DataDisplayComponent' using the Angular CLI command 'ng generate component data-display' or manually create the component files.
steps.hint: You can use the Angular CLI to quickly generate a component with all necessary files, or manually create a TypeScript file with the @Component decorator.
steps.expectedOutcome: A new Angular component named DataDisplayComponent is created with the proper @Component decorator and class definition.
successCriteria: DataDisplayComponent is created with @Component decorator, selector, and class definition.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the DataDisplayComponent. This component will be responsible for displaying the fetched data from our service.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started creating the component, but make sure it has the @Component decorator with selector, templateUrl/styleUrls, and the class is properly exported.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component wasn't created correctly. Remember to use the @Component decorator and export the class as DataDisplayComponent.

steps.title: Initialize component state for loading and data
steps.instruction: In your DataDisplayComponent class, add three properties: 'data' of type ApiResponse | null, 'loading' of type boolean, and 'error' of type string.
steps.hint: Define these properties inside the class body with appropriate type annotations and initial values.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component class will have typed properties to track fetched data, loading status, and error messages.
successCriteria: DataDisplayComponent has 'data', 'loading', and 'error' properties with correct TypeScript types and initial values.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully initialized the component state with proper TypeScript properties.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some properties, but make sure all three (data, loading, error) are present with correct types.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component doesn't have the required state properties. Add 'data', 'loading', and 'error' properties with appropriate types.

steps.title: Implement a fetch method in the component
steps.instruction: In your DataDisplayComponent class, create a method named 'fetchData' that will call the service method and update the component's loading and data properties.
steps.hint: Define a method inside the class that subscribes to the service's observable and handles the response.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now has a method that can fetch data from the service and update the component state.
successCriteria: The DataDisplayComponent class contains a method named 'fetchData' that subscribes to a service observable and updates component properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully implemented the fetchData method that will handle data fetching and state updates.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your fetchData method properly subscribes to the service and updates both the data and loading properties.
steps.feedbackWrong: The fetchData method is missing or doesn't follow the expected pattern. Review how to create methods in Angular components and subscribe to observables.

steps.title: Call the fetch method on component initialization
steps.instruction: In your DataDisplayComponent class, implement the ngOnInit lifecycle hook to call the fetchData method when the component loads.
steps.hint: Angular components can implement lifecycle hooks by importing OnInit from '@angular/core' and implementing the interface.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will automatically fetch data when it initializes, using Angular's lifecycle hooks.
successCriteria: DataDisplayComponent implements OnInit and calls fetchData within the ngOnInit method.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully implemented the ngOnInit lifecycle hook to fetch data automatically when the component loads.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've both implemented OnInit and called fetchData inside ngOnInit.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component doesn't yet fetch data on initialization. Remember to implement OnInit and call fetchData in ngOnInit.

steps.title: Create the component template structure
steps.instruction: In your DataDisplayComponent class, add a template property with basic HTML structure that includes *ngIf directives for loading, error, and data display states.
steps.hint: Use Angular's template property with backticks for multi-line strings. Include a loading message, error message, and data display section with appropriate *ngIf conditions.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example template with conditional rendering template: `
Loading...
{{ error }}
{{ data | json }}
`
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now has a template property with HTML structure that conditionally renders loading, error, and data states using *ngIf directives.
successCriteria: DataDisplayComponent has a template property containing HTML with *ngIf directives for loading, error, and data display states.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the template structure with conditional rendering for all three states.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some template structure, but make sure you include *ngIf directives for loading, error, AND data display states.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template structure is missing or doesn't include the required *ngIf directives for conditional rendering.

steps.title: Display fetched data in the template
steps.instruction: In the DataDisplayComponent's template property, use interpolation to display the fetched data's 'title' and 'message' properties when data is available.
steps.hint: Use double curly braces {{ }} to bind component properties to the template. Access the data object's properties like data.title and data.message.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component template will show the fetched data's title and message when data is available.
successCriteria: The template contains interpolation expressions for data.title and data.message inside the div element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully used interpolation to display the fetched data in the template. The data binding will automatically update when the component's data property changes.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using the correct property names (data.title and data.message) and proper interpolation syntax with double curly braces.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template doesn't yet display the fetched data. Remember to use interpolation {{ }} to bind the data properties to the template.
